text: A soldier that has faced many a defeat is less likely to just run away at the first sign of trouble.
See the scruffy one with the bandage and the limp? Pick that one. Just do it.
Nothing but tha best armour here-a! Quarrel tested! Money back guaranteed if it breaks!
You think that's scary? Wake me up when it starts spitting fire all over the pl-Alright, alright, bloody Myrmidia, I'm coming.
Keep 'em payments to the little buggers regular and they won't raze your city to the ground because you filed a couple of coins. Oh, Master Dwarf, what a lovely surprise!
The wealth of the Southern Realms flows through sea and land, into chests and pockets, and back again.
See here, we have to form up the troops into curved arrows and drive them deep into the enemy oblongs. What? Diagrams are clear.
In a heterogeneous mercenary army, coordination is key to victory. And a well-cooperating host is like an unstoppable grinder.
Actual war is only the last resort in the art of diplomacy, and leverage is just another kind of artillery.
When you are the one holding the lit candle for the surgeon to amputate your own leg, you got your troops full respect until the day you die.
Mercenaries know how to make their risky lives a little bit more sustainable. Surely not for the others.
The Cult of Myrmidia abhors Chaos in all its forms, and when it draws near, the Order of the Eagle must take arms.
By superior training - if not superior looks - the tercio can melt away any opposition by sheer efficiency of combined arms.
It can't be ignored - Tilea is the land of art, wealth and continuous warfare. Tilean mercenaries are highly valued for reasons beyond their funny accent.
The Border Confederacy is far from alien to aggressions. Countless greenskin and beastmen invasions tried to break them, unsuccessfully.
Those that come back from Lustria have plenty to tell about exotic beasts, incredible treasures and amazing scars. And know how to kill and plunder quickly and efficiently.
The inquisitorial Tribunals have little patience for petty concepts such as 'mercy', 'proof' and 'innocence'.
Devoid of flashy armour and banners of more famed regiments, the hardened border scouts fight a humble and endless struggle of their own.
After years of hardship, the Borderlands can finally prosper, their fighters defending not fearful towns but proud capitals.
By the union of impenetrable pike formations, daring cavalry actions and, of course, substantial economical support, Tilean warfare can reign supreme.

Inspired by the fabled might of Tylos, by the elven legacy and driven by the pent-up potential in the wealthy Tilea of nowadays, one might think of ways to overcome the usual tilean rivalry for something greater...
The jungle polishes the refugees, the brigands, the generic scallywags and even the honest (until proven otherwise) entrepreneurs into shrewd tough nuts. Or merciless despoilers.
The New World is a shrine of dangers and secrets, expensive ones. The most common trinket a bait to destruction or an unthinkable tool of power.
Following the unmistakable act of throwing crates of imported pasta (and the former Viceroy) in the harbour's waters, the thriving colonies start a new adventure entirely of their own.
Even as far as the New World, famous mercenaries can be persuaded to come, or even found locally.
Most Condottieri won't leave home without a company or two of toughened veterans. Others will want a jewel to their hat in the way of a famous regiment.
When the conditions and prospects of profit are right, even the expense behind recruiting and convincing the very best mercenaries in the Southern Realms can be justified...
The Borderlands have been Errantry War grounds for the Bretonnians. The bolsterous knights can definitely have uses if their wedges were pointed in the right direction.

Elector Counts can be persuaded to send a few regiments upon guarantees of protecting the southern borders for them, or to be conniving with their own politicking. Otherwise, you can always find a captain willing to volunteer for profit...
What do you mean you can't find troops? Look around, there's mercs everywhere! We're swimming in the buggers! You can't bloody walk around without sauntering into those wine-breaths!
Anybody can wash up in Tilea as a mercenary, and anybody with a talent for warfare can be put to use.

There may be an infinite resource in Tobaro and that is Ratmen in the deeps. Expanding the Deepwatch by using the tunnels as merciless training ground is exactly what Prince Piggalo would have done! Maybe.
With a few favours, the imperial expedition will certainly share some of their resources. We're all on the same side, aren't we?
Their attempt at a lustrian foothold didn't go particularly well, but just wave a few challenges and glories at a group of Bretonnians and you might soon have a lance with you.
We shouldn't let the imperial orders get ideas of independence. They were born here, they will return here. And know who's in charge.

If one could stack Leonardo da Miragliano's sketches in a pile, they'd probably reach Morrslieb. Upstart polymath Ugoletti has expressed interest in trying to make sense in one of these, so far kept secret. A wooden vehicle of bizarre shape, but the crank design looks all wrong...
The prototype seems to be somewhat working after bypassing Leonardo's puzzles, but Ugoletti needs more funding to improve the construction process and design. Your treasurers are murmuring.

Ugoletti claims that he can perfect the design, if only he could get his hands on an efficient power source; however, his sauce-splattered notes are exceedingly nebulous and he seems to be falling prey to hyperactive paranoia. If only one would fund an expedition to the jungles, for one of those things he calls Solar Engines...
Elves and Lizards don't know all monsters, and Man is one that is relentless.
The highlanders of the Irrana Mountains are renowned for their odd drinks and effective skirmishers.
These soldiers may appear out of touch and out of the loop with modern warfare, but they're far from ineffective.

We need to encourage the building of new chapterhouses in our territories if we want the support of the Myrmidian Orders, who so far considered the Border Princes not quite important enough. \\nThey weren't wrong, mind you.

Many are the tales of those lone riders, the somewhat-anti-heroes who head into the deep countryside to exact some sort of justice. Steel-eyed and quick-firing, often announced by the music of a carillon.
It's only natural for the South to invest money (albeit begrudgingly) in garrisons, considering the average neighbour is a scheming prince or a greenskin warband.
As noted in one of Leonardo's sketchbooks cryptically titled "!MOOB", it is a common misconception that fireworks only need go up. Of course, lighting them up on the crossbow is a bit of a thrill.
Sometimes you have to respectfully bow, break a casket of gold, and maybe bring a big golden scratching rake. \\nCall it an investment.
